2. Fair Work & Modern Slavery (Event-Specific) Compatible with PPN02 MAC 1e

Recommendation Overview Strengthen Modern Slavery prevention at call-off by encouraging active engagement, training and partnership approaches relevant to event delivery and stewarding supply chains.

Implementation Examples Supplier engagement with NGOs or human rights organisations Event-specific Modern Slavery risk briefings for managers and supervisors Independent advice to strengthen Modern Slavery Statements

Proposed Impact Reduces exploitation risks in high-risk event labour models Improves accountability beyond minimum compliance

Suggested Standard Reporting Metrics (KPIs) Optional “Stretch” KPIs Number of tier 1 and 2 suppliers who have been audited/assessed. Number of staff who have completed modern slavery training within 90 days of joining the organisation Number of NGOs or human rights organisations engaged Number of Modern Slavery training sessions delivered % of NGO recommendations implemented Number of collaborative initiatives undertaken

3. Community Engagement & Cultural Legacy Compatible with PPN02 MAC 3b

Recommendation Overview Use events as platforms for meaningful community participation, volunteering and celebration of local culture.

Implementation Examples Physical or digital community engagement hubs Local volunteering and employment pathways Showcasing local artists, performers and creatives

Proposed Impact Stronger community relationships Improved public perception of events Lasting cultural and social legacy

Suggested Standard Reporting Metrics (KPIs) Optional “Stretch” KPIs Number of engagement activities with the community, community representatives and or anchor institutions. % of local residents hired Community satisfaction survey scores Value of financial or in-kind contributions

4. Green Transport, Infrastructure & Logistics Compatible with PPN02 MACs 4a and 4b

Recommendation Overview Reduce environmental impact through low-carbon transport, green infrastructure and post-event legacy planning.

Implementation Examples Promote public transport, cycling and walking Incentivise low-emission travel for attendees and staff Repurpose temporary infrastructure for community use

Proposed Impact Lower event-related carbon emissions Improved urban environments Tangible community assets post-event

Suggested Standard Reporting Metrics (KPIs) Optional “Stretch” KPIs Annual reduction in carbon emissions arising from the performance of the contract, measured in metric tonnes carbon dioxide equivalents (MTCDE). Annual reduction in water use arising from the performance of the contract, measured in litres. Annual reduction in waste to landfill arising from the performance of the contract, measured in metric tonnes. % of attendees using low-emission transport % of structures powered by renewable energy % of materials sourced from sustainable or recycled sources % of infrastructure repurposed for community use Size of green spaces in m2 created under the contract, by the UK region.

5. Circular Economy, Energy & Resource Efficiency Compatible with PPN02 MACs 4a and 4b

Recommendation Overview Embed circular economy principles into event delivery to minimise waste, water and energy used

Implementation Examples Battery-first or low/zero carbon power solutions Energy and water requirement mapping Zero-waste commitments and reusable materials

Proposed Impact Reduced environmental footprint Cost efficiencies Strong sustainability assurance

Suggested Standard Reporting Metrics (KPIs) Optional “Stretch” KPIs Annual reduction in carbon emissions arising from the performance of the contract, measured in metric tonnes carbon dioxide equivalents (MTCDE). Annual reduction in water use arising from the performance of the contract, measured in litres. Annual reduction in waste to landfill arising from the performance of the contract, measured in metric tonnes. % of energy from renewable sources Waste sent to landfill (%) Planned vs actual energy and water usage Fuel consumption by type

6. Skills, Training & Employment Pathways Compatible with PPN02 MACs 1a, 1b, 1c and 1d

Recommendation Overview Use events to create longer-term employment and skills benefits, especially for young people and underrepresented groups.

Implementation Examples Partnerships with local colleges or training providers Event-relevant skills programmes (hospitality, logistics, security) Carbon Literacy training for staff

Proposed Impact Improved employability beyond the event Increased workforce resilience

Insurance requirements

Suppliers are required to maintain minimum insurance levels appropriate to their appointed lot. Higher insurance thresholds apply to Lot 1 due to the scale and risk profile of nationally significant events. Buyers must assess and define their own liability limits at the call-off stage.

Financial Requirement Lot 1 Lot 2 Lot 3, 4 & 5

Minimum Annual Turnover (Each of the last two financial years) £3,000,000 £1,000,000 none

Employer’s (Compulsory) Liability Insurance* £5,000,000 £5,000,000 £5,000,000

Public Liability Insurance £10,000,000 £1,000,000 £1,000,000

Professional Indemnity Insurance £10,000,000 £1,000,000 £1,000,000

Table 3: Insurance requirements

Procurement policy notes (PPNs)

Buyers must conduct their own internal assessment of which PPNs apply to their call-off contract, depending on scope and value. For a full list of PPNs, go to Procurement policy notes - GOV.UK.

Social value

Social value forms an important part of the EMF1 framework. The framework supports delivery of wider government priorities set out within Procurement Policy Note 002 (PPN002). DCMS encourages all Buyers to incorporate social value into their call-off procurements.

DCMS has developed a supporting document: Call-Off social value Buyer Toolkit (EMF1) - see Annex A of this Buyer Guide

The toolkit provides:

suggested social value themes

example award criteria

recommended KPIs

guidance on monitoring and reporting

Buyers may select the social value Model and associated KPIs most appropriate to their procurement. Suggested social value themes and KPIs are included within the Call-Off Social Value Buyer Toolkit.

Step 4 - Evaluation and selection

Buyers should evaluate supplier submissions against pre-defined ITT criteria.

Award criteria may include:

quality

price

social value

Evaluation records should be retained for audit purposes.

Buyers should determine the award criteria and their relative weightings based on the specific requirements, complexity, risk and desired outcomes of the call-off. Under the Procurement Act 2023 (PA23), there is no prescribed weighting between price and quality. Buyers should therefore consider the most appropriate balance to achieve the most advantageous tender (MAT) and value for money.

As a guide, Buyers may wish to consider the following indicative weighting ranges:

Award criterion Indicative weighting

Quality / technical solution 0%–100%

Price / cost 0%–100%

Social value Between 10% and 90% for central government, and 0% and 90% for wider public sector

Table 4: Award weighting

Buyers should determine the most appropriate weighting for their individual call-off, taking account of the specific requirements and applicable departmental policies and guidance.

Step 5 - Award and buy

Once evaluation is complete, Buyers may award the call-off contract. The successful supplier should be formally notified and appropriate records retained.

Where required, buyers should also issue standstill communications in accordance with applicable procurement rules.

All purchases under EMF1 must be completed through a call-off contract. Call-off contracts:

are separate agreements between the Buyer and Supplier

are based on the framework Call-Off templates

may include additional schedules and special terms where permitted

may extend beyond the expiry of the framework agreement

Buyers may:

amend template Call-Off Contracts where permitted

add additional schedules

introduce special terms or policies at the call-off stage; however, they must obtain their own legal advice before doing so

tailor KPIs and reporting requirements (please see annex A for our social value toolkit)

A call-off contract becomes legally binding once both parties have signed the call-off contract order form.

Expedited competitive selection process

For Lots 1, 2 and 3, buyers may issue an Expression of Interest (EOI) to framework suppliers. The EOI process enables buyers to:

test supplier availability and capacity

assess supplier interest

reduce the number of suppliers invited to tender

support efficient procurement timelines

The expedited competitive selection process can be used to alert suppliers of a short turn-around requirement.

Buyers should assess what a reasonable and proportionate timeframe they give to suppliers to reply to the EOI.

Only suppliers that respond positively to the EOI should be invited to submit a proposal or quotation.

Expedited competitive selection process leading to direct award

Where only one supplier responds positively to an EOI and remains eligible under the framework, the buyer may proceed with award without competition (or direct award).

Buyers must retain appropriate records and justification for any direct award decision.

Award without competition

Direct award may only be used where permitted under the framework terms and the Procurement Act 2023.

Under EMF1, direct award may be used:

for below-threshold requirements (up to £135,000 inclusive of VAT)

where urgency provisions under the Procurement Act 2023 apply

where an EOI exercise results in only one interested supplier

Direct award for urgency

Under Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023, Direct Award may be used where:

· the requirement is strictly necessary due to extreme and unavoidable urgency

· the urgency could not reasonably have been foreseen

· the urgency is not attributable to the Contracting Authority

Call-off terms

Main provisions of the call-off terms

The call-off terms for each of the Lots are fixed and contain the standard contract terms that are necessary to have in place between you and the supplier, including:

payment and invoicing
